chunks: From him, from Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Yaqub ibn Ja'far ibn Ibrahim Al-Ja'fari, who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who ties up an old horse, three sins are erased from him every day and eleven good deeds are written for him; and the one who ties up a hybrid horse, two sins are erased from him every day and seven good deeds are written for him; and the one who ties up a workhorse intending by it beauty, or fulfilling needs, or repelling an enemy from him, one sin is erased from him every day and six good deeds are written for him.'
ai.seo_question: What are the daily spiritual rewards for tying different types of horses according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith details the daily spiritual accounting for maintaining cavalry horses, reflecting the pre-modern military context where 'jihad' often involved mounted warfare. It distinguishes rewards based on the horse's quality and the specific intent—whether for general readiness, aesthetic display, or practical utility—highlighting the Shia emphasis on intention (niyyah) in transforming mundane acts into worship.

en.hubeali: From him, from Al Qasim Bin Yahya, from his grandfather Al Hassan Bin Rashid, from Yaqoub Bin Ja’far Bin Ibrahim Al Ja’fary who said,

‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who bridles an old horse, three sins are deleted from him during every days and there would be written for him eleven good deeds; and the one who bridles a hybrid (horse) there would be deleted from him two sins during every day and there would be written seven good deeds for him; and the one who bridles a work horse intending beauty by it, or fulfilment of needs, or repelling an enemy from him, there would be deleted one sin from him during every day, and there would be written six good deeds for him’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from his grandfather, al-Hassan ibn Rashid from Ya’qub ibn Ja’far ibn Ibrahim al-Ja’fariy who has said the following:

“I heard abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘If one maintains a horse of pure breed, three of his sins will be deleted every day and ten good deeds will be written in his favor. If one maintains a horse of mixed breed, two of his bad deeds will be deleted every day and seven good deeds will be written in his favor. If one maintains a mule for beauty or for his needs or use in his defense against the enemy, one of his sins will be deleted every day and six good deeds will be written in his favor.’”
